quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. This prevents you from moving into oncoming traffic if hit from behind. On hills, turn your wheels so your car will not roll into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: "No zones" around trucks are areas where cars:

options.text: Disappear in the truck's blind spots or are so close they prevent the driver from stopping and turning safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear in the truck's blind spots or are so close they prevent the driver from stopping and turning safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars disappear in a truck's or bus's blind spots. They can also be areas where cars are so close to a large vehicle that the driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "no zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Be aware of vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to give you the right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a car or between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their car before seeing you.

questions.question: What describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no breaks and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to handle them.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a motorcycle, give it a full lane. Never share the lane with a motorcycle. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights at night, do not look directly at them. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You may drive slower than the posted speed limit based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the limit. You must slow down for curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, and areas with animals or pedestrians.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken line is on your side, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center, you can pass from the side next to the broken line.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is allowed on a green arrow only.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming conditions like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What are crosswalks?

options.text: Always marked with lines on the pavement.
Either marked with lines or not marked at all.
Never marked with lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either marked with lines or not marked at all.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist whether they have lines or not. You must stop before a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. At what speed can this happen?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires can move water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of your traffic lane.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of your traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Lightly apply the brakes when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready for unexpected conditions.
Expect construction workers to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for unexpected conditions.
questions.explanation: In a construction zone, conditions can change quickly. Drive very carefully for your safety, the safety of other drivers, and the safety of construction workers.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: Only if you are in a crash.
If you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a crash or stopped for a traffic ticket.
questions.explanation: You must have proof of insurance with you when you drive. You must show proof of insurance and your license to a police officer when asked after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
Passing on the right is allowed when the road is clear.
Passing on the left is allowed when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is allowed when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass on the left when there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start from which lane?

options.text: Any lane (as long as it is safe).
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, start from the far left lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the highest legal speed for this road. You can drive slower if needed, but you cannot drive faster than the posted speed.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
It distracts other drivers around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your eyes, hands, and mind off the road. Even good drivers increase their crash risk by using a cell phone while driving.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass only from your direction.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from any direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go ahead if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around and do not drive forward.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: You must stop for them.
You do not have to stop for them.
You should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally or not at a crosswalk.

questions.question: At an intersection where all corners have stop signs, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who arrived first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: Vehicles go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before you enter the curve.
Slow down to the freeway speed limit.
Wait to brake until you are already in the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking while turning can cause your vehicle to skid.
